Princely Abbey of Corvey is located in Germany. Princely Abbey of Corvey is located in North Rhine-Westphalia. The **Princely Abbey of Corvey** (German: *Fürststift Corvey* or German: *Fürstabtei Corvey*) is a former Benedictine abbey and ecclesiastical principality now in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It was one of the half-dozen self-ruling *princely abbeys* of the Holy Roman Empire from the Late Middle Ages until 1792 when Corvey was elevated to a prince-bishopric. Originally built in 822 and 885 and remodeled in the Baroque period, the abbey is an exceptional example of Carolingian architecture, the oldest surviving example of a westwork, and the oldest standing medieval structure in Westphalia.
